items.title: Meta's new AI transcription model can distinguish between multiple speakers and languages in real-time
items.excerpt: Meta's Muse Voice Transcribe is its first real-time audio perception model, handling streaming multilingual transcription and separating overlapping speakers — the perception layer that on-device wearables like smart glasses need.

items.title: Perplexity's Hybrid Compute splits sensitive tasks between cloud and local AI
items.excerpt: Perplexity's new Hybrid Compute routes sensitive work to a local model on your machine while sending the rest to the cloud, making the on-device/cloud split a user-visible product decision.

items.title: 'Sonos 27' brings a refreshed UI to the app and lets AI agents control your system
items.excerpt: Sonos 27 redesigns the app UI and opens the speaker system to AI agents, turning a hardware ecosystem into something an assistant can drive directly.

items.title: Meta brings one of the Ray-Ban Display's most useful features to its standard smart glasses
items.excerpt: A flagship Ray-Ban Display capability trickles down to Meta's cheaper display-less smart glasses, narrowing the gap between tiers of AI eyewear.

items.title: RayNeo's new iO Smart Glasses slip a tiny display into your line of sight
items.excerpt: RayNeo's 33g iO Smart Glasses hide a monochrome MicroLED display in an everyday frame, offering live translation, 112-language dictation and an AI memory log for $479.

items.title: The Atlas 1.0 'Brain Wearable' Can Tell if You're Locked In
items.excerpt: Atlas' first $499 wearable EEG reads brain activity to tell wearers when they are in a focus state — a new sensing category aimed squarely at knowledge and creative work.

items.title: What to expect at IFA 2026: AI everywhere, robots, laptops evolved, smarter homes and more
items.excerpt: A preview of IFA 2026 in Berlin: Xiaomi's show debut, DJI's Romo 2 robot vacuums, TCL/RayNeo smart glasses and an AI-everywhere sweep across home and laptop hardware.

items.title: XREAL AURA Surpasses 10,000 Unit Reservations Ahead of Launch This Fall
items.excerpt: XREAL AURA, the first AR glasses running Google's Android XR, has passed 10,000 global reservations ahead of a $199 fall launch, signaling early demand from consumers, developers and enterprise.

items.title: Gemini Live gets productivity upgrade with Spark, Gmail, and other integrations
items.excerpt: Google significantly boosts Gemini Live with Spark, Gmail and other productivity integrations, pushing the always-listening assistant deeper into daily device workflows.

items.title: Microsoft Paint and Photos apps add invisible watermark to AI-generated content
items.excerpt: A developer reverse-engineered a server-issued GUID watermark that Windows Paint and Photos embed in every AI-generated image — including images made locally on Copilot+ PCs.

items.title: Homey Portal puts a physical dial on your smart home, and it looks pretty good
items.excerpt: Homey Portal is a round, dial-driven smart home controller that puts a tactile physical interface back in front of AI-managed home systems.

items.title: Google Pics is a Canva rival, and it's now available for all
items.excerpt: Google Pics, Workspace's 'pro-level' AI image creator and editor, hits general availability as a direct Canva competitor for everyday design work.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Voice Transcribe for real-time voice dictation on Mac
items.excerpt: Meta brings multilingual streaming transcription to the Mac via Muse Voice Transcribe, its first real-time audio perception model, making voice a first-class desktop input.

items.title: AirPods With Cameras Could Bring Improved Spatial Audio Head Tracking
items.excerpt: Code in macOS Tahoe 26.7 suggests Apple's camera-equipped AirPods will detect which display the wearer is looking at, extending spatial audio head tracking into visual sensing.

items.title: I gave my local LLM Adobe's closed-source converter, and it rebuilt the entire format from the bytes up
items.excerpt: Running GLM-5.3-Flash locally on a DGX Spark, the writer had an on-device model reverse-engineer an Adobe closed file format byte by byte — a look at what desktop-class local AI can now do.

items.title: Exclusive: Sonos CEO Tom Conrad on why Sonos software is now an 'operating system' and what its AI features mean
items.excerpt: Sonos CEO Tom Conrad explains why Sonos is '100% hardware and 100% software', why Ace Ultra needed new silicon, and how the new AI features try to serve both AI fans and skeptics.

items.title: Brand-new all-wheel-drive robotic lawn mowers with an extendable trimmer arm for seamless edge cutting
items.excerpt: Anthbot's R7 and R5 robotic mowers pair LiDAR navigation and all-wheel drive with an optional extendable trimmer arm, letting the robot finish edges no round chassis could reach.

items.title: Lenovo releases new desktop PC in the US with Intel Panther Lake and unusual design
items.excerpt: Lenovo's ThinkCentre X AIO Aura Edition builds on Intel's Panther Lake NPU silicon and adds an unusually tall display shaped for vertical multitasking.
